newsitem.title: USA: Refiners prop lackluster U.S. cash crude market.
newsitem.headline: Refiners prop lackluster U.S. cash crude market.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes increased in value for sweet Louisiana barrels on increased interest from U.S. Gulf Coast refiners, traders said Tuesday.
In general, the domestic grades failed to excite with only a few trades confirmed and most talk centered on the lack of initiative for moving barrels.
"The feature today is it's featureless," a trader said.
Outright crude returned to mark positive results, mainly on short covering moves putting the March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing 15 cents firmer at $22.50-60 a barrel.
March/April WTI remained steady from earlier at 33-35 cts.

Spot crude bumped higher on nervousness associated with reports of troop movements in Iraq towards the Iranian border. No U.S. confirmation of irregular activity was recorded, however, but nonetheless crude prices reacted, traders said.
Further on the grade front, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was valued at 26-30 cts over the WTI/Cushing, steady from earlier in the session, but slightly firmer from Friday.
"There were at least two refiners in there buying," said a trader, noting the refiners were expected to continue filling neglected needs in the coming days.

Increased arb openings may also be a large factor in the LLS market in coming sessions. The screen showed the WTI/Brent spread for April at more than $1.75, in the territory for making Brent an attractive play for the U.S. Gulf Coast.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was stolid, talked at flat to 15 cts under the WTI/Cushing.
West Texas Sour/Midland remained flat at $2.40-45 under the marker, and Eugene Island was valued around a $2.40 discount, traders said.
March Postings Plus has been done between $2.11-15, a few cents off the Friday levels.
Midland/WTI also stood still at a 40 cts discount to the WTI/Cushing.
